blocking.issue: The proposed amendment tells Data plane to drop the whole durable-state row. That row also holds the Plugin artifact cache `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/cache/oci/sha256/`, not only the wazero compiled-code directory. The owning document depends on that artifact cache: Hot-swap lifecycle step 1 fetches from it and step 7 recompiles from it on rollback. Foundation pack section 8.11 also lists Plugin artifacts as a disposable Node cache. Applied literally, the amendment removes a location that the owning document and the pack both rely on, so it contradicts them. The ADR also never mentions that pack section 8.11 lists 'compiled modules' as a persisted disposable cache, which is the same tension it reports for Data plane (the owning document tracks that under OQ-wasm-plugin-system-16).
blocking.evidence: ADR line 131: "Proposed owning-document amendment: [Data plane](../architecture/03-data-plane.md#durable-and-shared-state) still lists an on-disk `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/cache/wazero/` directory, which contradicts the in-memory-only rule; it SHOULD drop that row and close OQ-data-plane-11 with option (c)." Data plane line 40: "| Plugin artifacts; compiled Plugin code | `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/cache/oci/sha256/`; `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/cache/wazero/` | Disposable; refetched and verified, or recompiled |". Owning document, Hot-swap lifecycle: "1. **Fetch.** From the artifact cache or a pull by digest." and "7. **Retire.** ... a rollback recompiles from the artifact cache." Foundation pack section 8.11: "| Disposable caches | Under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`, layout owned by Data plane | Plugin artifacts and compiled modules; deleting them costs only warm-up |".
blocking.fix: Replace the last clause of line 131 with: "it SHOULD remove 'compiled Plugin code' and `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/cache/wazero/` from that row, keep `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}/cache/oci/sha256/` for Plugin artifacts, and close OQ-data-plane-11 with option (c). Foundation pack section 8.11 still names compiled code among disposable caches; that stays with OQ-wasm-plugin-system-16." This adds about 30 words. The body is about 1,400 of 1,500 words, so no other text needs trimming.

non_blocking.suggestion: "the only researched runtime that is pure Go" is imprecise, because Considered options also lists the pure-Go Extism go-sdk and mosn host (research section 2.1 marks both 'No' CGO for their wazero backends). Write "the only researched pure-Go runtime engine (the Extism go-sdk and mosn host wrap it)" instead.

"a Hot Reload that keeps a digest reuses its compiled code and pools" overstates the owning document. Pools carry over only when digest, canonical `config` and limits are all unchanged (Runtime rule 3, Hot-swap step 4). Write "reuses its compiled code, and unchanged pools carry over". Also cite cache.go ([source](https://github.com/wazero/wazero/blob/main/cache.go)) for sharing across runtimes; runtime.go documents only per-worker instantiation.

The owning document tags the accounting rule "4 × Wasm bytes per distinct digest and `limits.memoryBytes` (target)" in Default limits, and tags only the measured factor (hypothesis) in Performance model. Tag the accounting here as (target) and the factor as (hypothesis) so the two documents agree.
Add (target) to "at most max(1, `GOMAXPROCS`/4)" to match the owning document's Cold compilation row. The cited compilationworkers.go is an API reference, not a measurement.
